(born July 17, 1985) is an American professional [[basketball]] player for the [[Auckland Tuatara (basketball)|Auckland Tuatara]] of the New Zealand [[National Basketball League (New Zealand)|National Basketball League]] (NZNBL). He played college basketball for the [[LSU Tigers basketball|LSU Tigers]] before having multiple stints in the [[NBA]] between 2011 and 2013. ==High school and college== Born in [[Washington, D.C.]], Johnson attended [[Colonial Beach High School]] in [[Westmoreland County, Virginia]], where he averaged 22.2 points and 12.5 rebounds in his final season. He was then part of [[Laurinburg Institute]]'s prep school national championship team under coach Chris Chaney in 2005. He averaged 8.6 points, 3.9 rebounds and 2.7 blocks per game as a senior and shot 42 percent from three-point range.{{cite web|url=https://lsusports.net/sports/mens-basketball/roster/chris-johnson/3023|title=Chris Johnson|work=lsusports.net|date=8 July 2019 |access-date=April 21, 2021}} Johnson played college basketball for the [[LSU Tigers basketball|LSU Tigers]] from 2005 to 2009. In 85 games, he made 59 starts and averaged 7.2 points, 5.2 rebounds and 2.0 blocks in 20.4 minutes per game.{{cite web|url=https://www.sports-reference.com/cbb/players/chris-johnson-2.html|title=Chris Johnson|work=sports-reference.com|access-date=April 21, 2021}} With 176 blocks, he finished his four-year career as the second [[LSU Tigers basketball statistical leaders|all-time leader in blocked shots]] at LSU behind [[Shaquille O'Neal]] (412). ==Professional career== ===2009–10 season=== After going undrafted in the [[2009 NBA draft]], Johnson joined the [[New Jersey Nets]] for the [[NBA Summer League]].{{cite web|url=http://www.nba.com/nets/news/2009SummerLeague.html |title=NETS: 2009 Summer League |work=NBA.com |accessdate=January 8, 2010 |url-status=dead |archiveurl=https://web.archive.org/web/20140203021310/http://www.nba.com/nets/news/2009SummerLeague.html |archivedate=February 3, 2014 }} He started the 2009–10 season in Turkey with [[Aliağa Petkim]] before ending the season in Poland with [[Turów Zgorzelec]].{{cite web|url=http://www.sportando.com/en/cat/nba/79571/turow-tabs-chris-johnson.html|title=Turow tabs Chris Johnson|work=Sportando.com|date=January 8, 2010|accessdate=January 8, 2010}} ===2010–11 season=== After a quick pre-season stint with the [[Boston Celtics]],{{cite web|url=https://basketball.realgm.com/player/Chris-Johnson/Summary/1655|title=Chris Johnson|work=RealGM.com|access-date=April 21, 2021}} Johnson joined the [[Dakota Wizards]] of the [[NBA D-League]]. In 35 games for the Wizards during the 2010–11 season, he averaged 16.2 points, 9.2 rebounds, 1.3 assists and 2.8 blocks per game. On January 24, 2011, Johnson signed a 10-day contract with the [[Portland Trail Blazers]].{{cite web|title=TRAIL BLAZERS SIGN CENTER CHRIS JOHNSON|url=http://www.iamatrailblazersfan.com/PressReleaseDisplay/tabid/297/ItemID/2238/Default.aspx|work=NBA.com|date=January 24, 2011|accessdate=January 24, 2011|url-status=usurped|archiveurl=https://web.archive.org/web/20110130214142/http://www.iamatrailblazersfan.com/PressReleaseDisplay/tabid/297/ItemID/2238/Default.aspx|archivedate=January 30, 2011}} A month later, he signed a 10-day contract with the Celtics.{{cite web|url=https://www.espn.com/blog/boston/celtics/post?id=4681069|title=C's ink Johnson to 10-day contract|work=ESPN.com|date=February 24, 2011|access-date=February 24, 2011}} On March 14, he re-signed with the Trail Blazers for the remainder of the 2010–11 season.{{cite web |title=TRAIL BLAZERS SIGN CENTER CHRIS JOHNSON FOR REMAINDER OF SEASON |url=http://www.iamatrailblazersfan.com/PressReleaseDisplay/tabid/297/ItemID/2373/Default.aspx |work=NBA.com |date=March 14, 2011 |accessdate=March 14, 2011 |url-status=usurped |archiveurl=https://web.archive.org/web/20110317103221/http://www.iamatrailblazersfan.com/PressReleaseDisplay/tabid/297/ItemID/2373/Default.aspx |archivedate=March 17, 2011 }} ===2011–12 season=== During the [[2011 NBA lockout]], Johnson played for and won a championship in the Dominican Republic with [[Leones de Santo Domingo]] of the [[Liga Nacional de Baloncesto]] (LNB).{{cite web|url=http://www.oregonlive.com/blazers/index.ssf/2011/11/rip_city_basketball_classic_no.html|title=Rip City Basketball Classic notes: Wesley Matthews healthy, Jamal Crawford lobbies to be a Trail Blazer and Chris Johnson details Dominican adventure|work=OregonLive.com|last=Freeman|first=Joe|date=November 7, 2011|accessdate=November 8, 2011}} Following the lockout, he re-joined the Trail Blazers for the 2011–12 season. League|Las Vegas Summer League]]. ===2017–18 season=== Between June and October 2017, Johnson played in China for the [[Anhui Dragons]] of the [[National Basketball League (China)|NBL]].{{cite web|url=https://basketball.australiabasket.com/player/Chris-Johnson/New-Zealand/Auckland-Tuatara/89667|title=Chris Johnson|work=australiabasket.com|access-date=April 9, 2026|url-access=subscription}} He then moved to Croatia for the 2017–18 season to play for [[KK Cedevita|Cedevita Zagreb]]. ===2018–19 season=== Between October 2018 and January 2019, Johnson played in Lebanon for [[Homenetmen Beirut B.C.]] In April 2019, he played for [[Shabab Al Ahli]] during the [[FIBA Asia Champions Cup]] GBA Qualifiers. ===2019–20 season=== Johnson returned to Shabab Al Ahli for the 2019–10 season.{{cite web|url=https://www.asia-basket.com/United-Arab-Emirates/news/595985/Johnson-comes-back-to-Shabab-Al-Ahli|title=Johnson comes back to Shabab Al Ahli|work=asia-basket.com|date=September 12, 2019|access-date=April 21, 2021}} In January 2020, he moved to Japan to play for [[SeaHorses Mikawa]]. ===2020–21 season=== In March 2021, Johnson had a short stint in Bahrain with [[Al-Muharraq SC]]. On April 20, 2021, Johnson signed with the [[Auckland Huskies]] for the [[2021 New Zealand NBL season]].{{cite web|url=https://aucklandhuskies.co.nz/huskies-sign-former-nba-big-man-chris-johnson/|title=Huskies Sign Former NBA Big Man Chris Johnson|work=aucklandhuskies.co.nz|date=April 20, 2021|access-date=April 21, 2021|url-status=dead|archive-url=https://web.archive.org/web/20210518193446/https://aucklandhuskies.co.nz/huskies-sign-former-nba-big-man-chris-johnson/|archive-date=May 18, 2021}} He left the Huskies on July 8 to return to the United States to play in the [[Big3]] league.{{cite web|last=Hinton|first=Marc|url=https://www.stuff.co.nz/sport/basketball/300352542/auckland-huskies-nbl-title-ambitions-take-a-hit-with-departure-of-chris-johnson|title=Auckland Huskies' NBL title ambitions take a hit with departure of Chris Johnson|work=Stuff.co.nz|date=July 8, 2021|access-date=July 10, 2021}} He averaged 20.1 points, 11.0 rebounds, 2.9 assists and 1.7 blocks per game with the Huskies. ===2021–22 season=== After a stint in the Dominican Republic with Parque Hostos, Johnson moved to Saudi Arabia in December 2021 to play for [[Al-Nassr BC]]. In 15 games, he averaged 25.1 points, 15.7 rebounds, 3.7 assists and 1.7 blocks per game. On April 21, 2022, Johnson signed with the [[Auckland Tuatara (basketball)|Auckland Tuatara]] for the [[2022 New Zealand NBL season]], returning to the rebranded Auckland franchise.{{cite web|url=https://tuatarabasketball.com/former-nba-star-chris-johnson-joins-tuatara/|title=FORMER NBA STAR CHRIS JOHNSON JOINS TUATARA|work=aucklandhuskies.co.nz|date=April 21, 2022|access-date=April 21, 2022}} He left the team mid-season to return to the Big3 league, but then returned to the Tuatara for the final regular season game and finals.{{cite web|url=https://tuatarabasketball.com/hes-back-johnson-returns-to-boost-tuatara/|title=HE'S BACK – JOHNSON RETURNS TO BOOST TUATARA|work=aucklandhuskies.co.nz|date=August 2, 2022|access-date=August 2, 2022}} ===2022–23 season=== On August 23, 2022, Johnson signed with [[Taipei Fubon Braves]] of the [[P. League+]].{{Cite news|url=https://sportando.basketball/en/taipei-fubon-braves-inks-chris-johnson/|title=Taipei Fubon Braves inks Chris Johnson|last=|first=|date=August 23, 2022|website=|newspaper=Sportando|language=En|access-date=August 23, 2022|last1=Skerletic |first1=Dario }} ===2023–24 season=== Johnson returned to Taipei Fubon Braves for the 2023–24 season. ===2024–25 season=== On July 24, 2024, Johnson signed with [[New Taipei Kings]] of the [[Taiwan Professional Basketball League]] (TPBL).{{cite web|title=TPBL》富邦勇士FMVP強森離隊 竟然轉投新北國王|url=https://sports.ltn.com.tw/news/breakingnews/4746869|website=Liberty Times Net|date=July 24, 2024|access-date=July 24, 2024}} On April 3, 2025, Johnson was not registered in the [[2024–25 TPBL season]] final rosters.{{cite news|title=TPBL最終註冊名單公佈 7隊洋將正式底定 |url=https://sports.ettoday.net/news/2936920 |accessdate=April 3, 2025 |work=ETtoday |date=April 3, 2025 }} But Johnson would play for [[2025 Basketball Champions League Asia-East]].{{cite news|title=國王確定4洋將陣容 遺珠強森續戰BCL |url=https://udn.com/news/story/7003/8650955 |accessdate=April 3, 2025 |work=United Daily News |date=April 3, 2025 }} On June 8, New Taipei Kings announced that Johnson had left the team.{{cite news |url=https://www.chinatimes.com/realtimenews/20250608002116-260403?chdtv |title=BCL階段性任務結束 新北國王宣布強森離隊返美 |date=June 8, 2025 |work=China Times |access-date=June 8, 2025 }} ===2025–26 season=== In January 2026, Johnson joined [[Al-Nassr BC]] in Saudi Arabia. On April 9, 2026, Johnson signed with the [[Auckland Tuatara (basketball)|Auckland Tuatara]] for the [[2026 New Zealand NBL season]], returning to the franchise for a third stint.{{cite news
